title: Three Real Roots of a Depressed Cubic
originalTopic: Locating and approximating all real roots of a cubic
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find how many real roots the equation x^3 - 3x + 1 = 0 has and approximate each of them. A narrow window can make two of the crossings look like one.

steps.title: Use the turning points to count roots
steps.explanation: The local maximum value is positive and the local minimum value is negative, so the curve must cross the axis three times.
steps.why: Opposite signs at the two turning points is the cleanest certificate that a cubic has three distinct real roots.

steps.title: Bracket each root separately
steps.explanation: Each pair of sign changes isolates one root in (-2, -1), in (0, 1) and in (1, 2).
steps.why: Separate brackets prevent the solver from converging to the same root three times, a common failure mode with one shared starting guess.

steps.title: Refine numerically
steps.explanation: Zooming each bracket or applying a root-finder gives the three values, which are exactly 2 cos 160 degrees, 2 cos 80 degrees and 2 cos 40 degrees.
steps.why: Recognizing the trigonometric form explains why the roots are irrational yet expressible, and gives an independent check on the decimals.

steps.title: Check with the window
steps.explanation: This window displays the peak at (-1, 3), the valley at (1, -1) and all three crossings at once.
steps.why: Seeing both turning points and all crossings in one frame confirms the count of three roots graphically as well as analytically.
